integrity: The source reduction to at most m+1 endpoint-derived Schur permutahedra was checked directly. Permutation invariance forces the unique minimum-enclosing center to the diagonal. Consecutive layer radii differ by a signed midpoint threshold, so the entire high-dimensional problem collapses exactly to a strongly convex one-variable far-endpoint function. A piecewise-quadratic derivative calculation gives the finite scan, and an independent numerical ambient-space replay corroborates deterministic cases.
scientific_limitations: The theorem applies to the Newton polytopes of good symmetric polynomials through the endpoint-layer structure proved in the primary source. It determines the Euclidean minimum enclosing sphere and contact source orbits, not the inradius, John ellipsoid, or arbitrary symmetric Newton polytopes.
title: Good symmetric Newton polytopes have an exact one-dimensional minimum-sphere formula
